newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban battle foes in northwest Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Taleban battle foes in northwest Afghanistan.

text.p: Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban movement on Wednesday reported heavy overnight fighting against forces loyal to Uzbek militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum in the northwestern province of Badghis.

A Taleban spokesman contacted by telephone in the western city of Herat told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) the Taleban had killed nine Dostum soldiers and captured 70 in overnight battles in the northern Ghormach district, about 20 km (13 miles) inside Badghis.
The spokesman said several hundred Taleban fighters had been sent recently to reinforce the fast-changing front line.
The Taleban captured Ghormach and Murghab in Badghis and the Qaysar district in the adjacent province of Faryab when they began an offensive against Dostum late last week.
The Taleban spokesman's report that fighting was now going on in Ghormach confirmed reports from Kabul on Tuesday that Dostum's forces had driven the Islamic militants back.

Kabul-based sources said on Tuesday that 2,000 men sent by Dostum under General Malik (one name) to meet the threat on a new front had counter-attacked on Sunday, seizing the town of Murghab, some 60 km (40 miles) inside Badghis province.
Acting Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told a news conference in Kabul on Tuesday that Badghis was calm and "big changes will happen in the north in the very near future".
He said most commanders in the region had close links with the Taleban and would soon rise against Dostum.

If Dostum could recapture Badghis, he would be in a position to threaten the western city of Herat where there is a big population of ethnic Tajiks, cousins to the people of Dostum ally Ahmad Shah Masood, the ousted government military chief.
An AIP correspondent in Herat on Sunday saw 19 weak and exhausted prisoners in the city's central jail.
Taleban officials said they were among more than 300 pro-Dostum fighters captured in recent clashes. Several of the 19 said they had been forced to fight.
One prisoner, named Hayat (one name), said he had been forcibly conscripted by Dostum. He said he was among 200 fighters who had surrendered to the Taleban at Morghab.
